# std.deque

<!-- Generated by `badger doc std` from the checked interfaces (badger 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

Double-ended queues: a persistent banker's deque. `push_front`,
`push_back`, `pop_front`, and `pop_back` take amortized O(1); every
operation returns a new deque and leaves the old one unchanged.

    let d = deque.empty<Int>().push_back(1).push_back(2).push_front(0)
    let (first, rest) = d.pop_front().unwrap_or((-1, d))   // 0

## Types

### `Deque`

```badger
struct Deque<T> { front: deque.Cons<T>, front_len: Int, back: deque.Cons<T>, back_len: Int }
```

A deque: `front` holds the first elements in order, `back` the last in
reverse; each side is rebuilt from the other when it runs out.
